authorities.name: Competition Act 1998, s.18 - Chapter II prohibition
authorities.date_note: Enactment year. The text verified this session is the current in-force version; the page notes pending amendments from 2023 c.28 and 2026 asc 7 not yet incorporated into s.18 itself.
authorities.proposition: Conduct by one or more undertakings amounting to abuse of a dominant position in a market is prohibited if it may affect trade within the UK (s.18(1)), subject to s.19. Non-exhaustive examples of abuse include directly or indirectly imposing unfair purchase or selling prices or other unfair trading conditions (s.18(2)(a)) - the 'Chapter II prohibition' (s.18(4)).
authorities.verification_note: Fetched live and directly this session, independently re-fetched and re-confirmed a second time - both fetches consistent on s.18(1)'s exact text.

authorities.name: Napp Pharmaceutical Holdings Ltd v Director General of Fair Trading
authorities.judge_or_panel: Sir Christopher Bellamy (President), Barry Colgate, Professor Peter Grinyer
authorities.proposition: Applying the Chapter II prohibition (via the s.60 consistency obligation with EU case law), pricing below average variable cost to hospitals was held abusive per se (adopting the AKZO/Tetra Pak II test), without requiring proof of specific intent to eliminate competition. The Tribunal articulated a 'super-dominance' principle: because Napp held around 95% of the relevant market (far above the roughly 50% in AKZO), the below-average-variable-cost-pricing-is-abusive rule applies with even more force, not less, to such a near-monopolist. The Tribunal substantially upheld the underlying regulator's decision on liability.
authorities.verification_note: The case's identity (name, citation, tribunal, date, panel) is independently confirmed via the Competition Appeal Tribunal's own official case page and a GOV.UK official case summary - both consistent with the researching agent's own direct read of the judgment PDF. The specific 'super-dominance'/paragraph 228 quote rests on that agent's PDF read alone; this session's own tools could not decode the same PDF to independently reproduce the exact wording, so this specific quote is recorded as VERIFIED_SECONDARY_SOURCE rather than primary, pending a direct human read of the CAT judgment.

edges.verified_via: Napp Pharmaceutical Holdings Ltd v Director General of Fair Trading [2002] CAT 1, applying the Chapter II prohibition to below-cost pricing by a near-monopolist supplier.
